newsitem.title: USA: Northeast Utilities to sell Charter Oak.
newsitem.headline: Northeast Utilities to sell Charter Oak.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said on Tuesday that it plans to sell Charter Oak Energy Inc, a subsidiary that develops independent power production facilities.

Northeast Utilities said it has decided to sell Charter Oak because it no longer fits with the company's core business strategy of being a energy and energy services provider in the northeastern United States.
Charter Oak was formed in 1988 to invest in independent power projects outside the company's service territory, Northeast Utilities said.
Northeast Utilities said it had about $70 million of equity invested in Charter Oak.

Separately, Northeast Utilities said its board of trustees voted to suspend payment of the company's common stock dividend, effective in the second quarter. The company's management recommended the move in an announcement it had made Monday.

Northeast Utilities said suspension of the dividend was the result of ongoing outages at its Millstone nuclear power plant and the state-ordered restructuring of the electrical power business in New Hampshire.
Suspending the dividend will enable Northeast Utilities to conserve about $130 million annually.
The company's dividend payable on March 31, 1997 will not be affected by the suspension, Northeast Utilities said.
